summary.text: Joel McEntire is a Republican member of the Washington House of Representatives for District 19-Position 2, in office since January 11, 2021, and he is running for re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election against Democrat Terry Carlson.
A former middle-school teacher and a U.S. Marine Corps reservist, he is serving his third term.

paragraphs.text: McEntire was raised in Cathlamet and graduated from Wahkiakum High School in 2006, according to his House Republican biography.
He served a two-year mission in Cleveland, Ohio, then served in the U.S. Marine Corps, and he continues as a Marine Corps reservist.
He holds a Bachelor of Science degree in evolutionary ecology and a master's degree in mathematics education, and he worked as a full-time teacher at John C. Thomas Middle School in Cathlamet.
McEntire succeeded Democrat Brian Blake in the 19th District seat.

His biography lists his priorities as protecting the fishing, farming and forestry industries of Southwest Washington, reducing the cost of living, making communities safer and addressing affordable housing.
He and his wife, Margaret Jean, married in 2010 and have five children.

On September 14, 2026, a Cowlitz County District Court judge granted a year-long protection order against McEntire, sought by a Longview resident over comments he made to her on Facebook, and found that two of the comments were not protected by the First Amendment, according to The Daily Chronicle.
McEntire argued that his posts were protected speech.

The Chronicle also reported that on September 2, 2026, the Washington State Legislative Ethics Board fined him $500, with $250 suspended, finding that he had threatened to use his position to access confidential information about a constituent.

sources.title: Rep. Joel McEntire hit with no-contact order linked to conduct on social media
